observations: Activator execute checks held-item tags/static exception-derived blacklist and configured filter before fake-player position/face/sneak/hand setup. Action enum input is directly indexed from NBT. Action success alone controls buffer replacement and subsequent extra-inventory drops. Item/block use falls back from useItemOn to useItem and uses consumesAction; interacting with a selected entity also uses consumesAction. These are request-level results, not independently confirmed world settlement.

Attack chooses one LivingEntity under tag/filter and nearest/random/round-robin policy first. If that selected entity is a Player and router has security upgrades and isPermitted(player), execute refuses this attack; it does not select another candidate. Otherwise fakePlayer.attack is invoked and the method returns true without inspecting actual damage outcome. Round-robin increments its index before choosing. Predicate arrangement is supporting context, not a separate owner or new immune family.

Accepted migration owner8411 already owns durable security-upgrade Owner/Players, upgrade inventory, derived UUID set, owner GameProfile and fake-player rebuild. Its complete judgment expressly did not expand final Activator attacks. This screen adds the actual downstream selected-player refusal boundary but does not award that follow-up another persistence owner.

Use exceptions inspect stack-method names and may add the held item or hit block to process-global static sets, then log. No own reset or NBT recovery is present in this class. This is failure-derived quarantine, not proven Boss immunity or final rejection feedback. It is not counted as a new mechanism.

Extruder successful placement state precedes buffer extraction, extension-distance/data update and sound request, then entity push. Pushing can be disabled by config. It selects entities within the placed-block AABB and skips pistonPushReaction IGNORE; remaining entities receive replacement velocity from facing and speedaugment, onGround false, collision flags false, and living jumping true. This is not a damage/knockback acceptance receipt. Retraction of empty/liquid space can decrement distance while returning false.

PushEntityMessage carries entity integerID and three doubles, then on client looks up current-world entity and replaces velocity, clears collision flags and sets living jumping; it does not mirror server onGround=false. The visible receiver has an entity null gate but no world-null guard, UUID/dimension/sequence/source identity, or final motion acceptance test. TRACKING_ENTITY distribution is requested; self-player delivery and platform transport implementation are not established here.

RouterFakePlayer tick maintains attackStrengthTicker and updates old/new mainhand attribute modifiers when configured and stack changed. It is silent and uses getY for eyeY. Extra-inventory drop loop stops at first empty slot; spawned-item result is ignored before clearing each visited slot. These are limitations, not separate immune references.

Comparison with complete Lycanites instability judgment separates final control exclusion and independent client impulse from damage acceptance. Generic velocity sync, piston predicate and configurable speed are not enough to establish a new semantically distinct whole control policy here. Both examined branches remain0; no candidate awaiting credit.
